capabilities.title: Versioned bounded JSON framing
capabilities.behavior: Frames hypermid.v1 JSON with a four-byte big-endian length, rejects bodies above 8 MiB, and chunks event data at 64 KiB with digest verification.
acceptance: Oversize and malformed frames are rejected before declared-body allocation.
Chunk order, count, and SHA-256 digest are verified before event publication.

capabilities.title: Authenticated local and external sessions
capabilities.behavior: Binds local sessions to owner credentials and supervised spawn identity while keeping external access opt-in behind TLS and scoped principals.
acceptance: Proof binds both nonces, protocol, daemon instance, and connection class.
An external session without trusted TLS identity and required scopes is refused.

capabilities.title: Validated module manifests
capabilities.behavior: Discovers manifests only from configured roots and validates identity, artifact digest, dependencies, capabilities, policy, and launch proof before routing.
acceptance: Invalid manifests do not change the registry generation.
A process is unroutable until launch identity and catalog validation succeed.
Every declared system role runs on the local fabric without a foreign service.

capabilities.title: Epoch-safe route lifecycle
capabilities.behavior: Reserves and binds routes atomically, stamps each binding epoch, and closes routes when process, capability, or scope authority changes.
acceptance: A route appears only after module bind acknowledgement.
Frames from an earlier epoch never reach a reused route slot.

capabilities.title: Per-route flow control
capabilities.behavior: Uses independent request and byte credits with bounded queues and a separately bounded control lane.
acceptance: Credit exhaustion remains isolated to its route.
Terminal frames release request credits without queue or ledger leaks.

capabilities.title: Cancellation and deadlines
capabilities.behavior: Carries one absolute deadline through every hop and settles idempotent cancellation races with one terminal outcome.
acceptance: Internal hops and retries never extend the original deadline.
Cancel, completion, timeout, and disconnect races emit at most one terminal result.

capabilities.title: Contained process supervision
capabilities.behavior: Runs every module through a bounded lifecycle with platform process containment, restart backoff, ordered drains, and orphan cleanup by stable process identity.
acceptance: Crash loops respect the restart window and backoff ceiling.
Daemon recovery never kills a process whose pid was reused with a different identity.

capabilities.title: Safe module replacement
capabilities.behavior: Previews registry reconciliation and performs exclusive or overlap-safe replacement without routing to an unready candidate.
acceptance: Failed warmup leaves the incumbent serving.
Successful cutover rejects new work on the incumbent before its drain begins.

capabilities.title: Durable effect recovery
capabilities.behavior: Commits effect intent before dispatch, commits outcomes before acknowledgement, deduplicates by effect id and input digest, and reconciles after restart.
acceptance: Repeated effect ids with another digest are refused.
Ambiguous recovery yields unknown and never blind replay.

capabilities.title: Durable scoped event bus
capabilities.behavior: Persists scoped events with cursors and supports snapshot, replay, live continuation, durable acknowledgement, redelivery, and dead-letter handling.
acceptance: Publish and subscribe both enforce principal scope.
Expired cursors and lagged consumers receive explicit recovery positions.

capabilities.title: Health and diagnostics
capabilities.behavior: Combines readiness, probes, resources, route state, dependencies, stderr, terminal history, provenance, and spawn events into inspectable evidence.
acceptance: Diagnostics remain readable during module failure.
Unsupported and unavailable evidence is explicit rather than encoded as zero or healthy.

capabilities.title: Scoped control RPC
capabilities.behavior: Provides typed describe, registry, route, supervisor, effect, and event operations with idempotent mutations and generation-stamped responses.
acceptance: Every operation checks its named principal scope.
Subscriptions reject foreign or expired cursors with recovery data.

capabilities.title: Owned install update and uninstall
capabilities.behavior: Uses signed release metadata, digest-verified staged activation, rollback, and an ownership ledger to protect user and unrelated state.
acceptance: Untrusted, stale, incompatible, or digest-mismatched artifacts never activate.
Uninstall deletes only still-matching ownership-ledger paths.

capabilities.title: Cross-platform daemon service lifecycle
capabilities.behavior: Registers the per-user daemon with native service managers while preserving ordered shutdown of supervised children.
acceptance: Definitions restart on unexpected daemon exit and allow the full drain ceiling.
Service-manager refusal text reaches the caller without replacement by a generic error.

capabilities.title: Opt-in federated routing
capabilities.behavior: Pairs peers, validates signed candidates, dials direct before relay, establishes mutually authenticated encryption, and intersects remote grants with local policy.
acceptance: Relay grants are side-specific, single-use, and expire.
Only explicitly remote operations are discoverable or callable across peers.

capabilities.title: Durable outbound phone channel
capabilities.behavior: Uses outbound-only encrypted federation, a durable local mutation log, reconnect reconciliation, and content-free wake notifications.
acceptance: A reconnect reconciles unsettled mutations before another mutation is admitted.
Wake notifications contain only an opaque token and cannot invoke an operation.

capabilities.title: Typed Gideon adapter
capabilities.behavior: Provides typed asynchronous control, route, event, cancellation, and effect-status calls using shared contract definitions.
acceptance: Daemon epoch changes invalidate routes and event cursors before reuse.
The adapter retries only retryable queries within the original deadline and never blindly retries durable effects.
